chenla.name: Chenla
chenla.summary: A Chinese name for a kingdom, vassal to Funan, that existed in Indochina from the late 6th to early 9th century, preceding the Khmer Empire; historians debate whether it was ever a single unified state.

funan.name: Funan
funan.summary: A loose network of ancient Indianized states in what is now Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam, existing from the 1st to 7th century CE, generally considered the first known kingdom in Southeast Asia.

shailendra-dynasty.name: Shailendra dynasty
shailendra-dynasty.summary: An Indianised dynasty ruling 8th-century Java that promoted Mahayana Buddhism and built monuments including Borobudur, and that also controlled parts of maritime Southeast Asia and, for a time, Srivijaya.

kedu-plain.name: Kedu Plain
kedu-plain.summary: A fertile volcanic plain in Central Java between four volcanoes, corresponding to today's Magelang and Temanggung regencies, long central to Javanese history including the Sailendra dynasty and Borobudur.

khmer-people.name: Khmer people
khmer-people.summary: An ethnic group native to Cambodia making up over 95% of its population, predominantly Theravada Buddhist, with related communities in Thailand and Vietnam's Mekong Delta.

pallava-dynasty.name: Pallava dynasty
pallava-dynasty.summary: A dynasty ruling parts of southern India from 275 to 897 CE, reaching its height under Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I and known for patronizing Hindu temple architecture and the Pallava script.

borobudur.name: Borobudur
borobudur.summary: A 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in Central Java, Indonesia, decorated with thousands of relief panels and originally hundreds of Buddha statues, built under the Sailendra dynasty.

khmer-empire.name: Khmer Empire
khmer-empire.summary: A Southeast Asian empire centered on Angkor in what is now Cambodia, lasting from 802 to 1431 CE and ruling much of mainland Southeast Asia before likely collapsing due to droughts and floods damaging its water infrastructure.

royal-ballet-of-cambodia.name: Royal Ballet of Cambodia
royal-ballet-of-cambodia.summary: A classical Khmer dance tradition tied to the royal court, performed at coronations, weddings and funerals, which nearly disappeared under the Khmer Rouge but is now UNESCO-listed heritage.

apsara-dance.name: Apsara Dance
apsara-dance.summary: A traditional Cambodian dance performed by women with graceful, codified gestures narrating classical myths or religious stories; one of Cambodia's national symbols.

ng-quy-n.name: Ngô Quyền
ng-quy-n.summary: Warlord (898–944) who founded the Ngô dynasty after defeating the Southern Han at the Battle of Bạch Đằng River in 938, ending 1,000 years of Chinese rule over Vietnam.

battle-of-b-ch-ng-938.name: Battle of Bạch Đằng River
battle-of-b-ch-ng-938.summary: A 938 naval battle near Hạ Long Bay in which Vietnamese forces under Ngô Quyền defeated Chinese Southern Han troops, ending centuries of Chinese rule and marking a turning point in Vietnamese history.

southern-han.name: Southern Han
southern-han.summary: A dynastic state of southern China (917 to 971) controlling modern Guangdong and Guangxi during the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period; it tried and failed to annex Vietnam's Jinghai.

ng-dynasty.name: Ngô dynasty
ng-dynasty.summary: Semi-independent Vietnamese dynasty from 939 to 968, founded by Ngô Quyền after his 938 victory over the Chinese Southern Han at the Battle of Bạch Đằng River.

tri-u-vi-t-v-ng.name: Triệu Việt Vương
tri-u-vi-t-v-ng.summary: King of the Vietnamese Early Lý dynasty in the 6th century, born Triệu Quang Phục; co-ruler from 548 and sole ruler from 555 until his death in 571, known for leading guerrilla resistance against the Liang dynasty.

liang-dynasty.name: Liang dynasty
liang-dynasty.summary: Imperial dynasty of southern China (502–557), one of the Southern dynasties, preceded by the Southern Qi and succeeded by the Chen dynasty.

emperor-wu-of-liang.name: Emperor Wu of Liang
emperor-wu-of-liang.summary: Founding emperor of the Chinese Liang dynasty (464–549), whose long reign was one of the most stable and prosperous of the Southern dynasties. He patronized Buddhism and the arts before a rebellion ended his rule.

early-l-dynasty.name: Early Lý dynasty
early-l-dynasty.summary: A Vietnamese dynasty ruling from 544 to 602 CE, founded by Lý Bí, who proclaimed himself emperor and named his realm Vạn Xuân, 'Myriad Spring'.

l-nam.name: Lý Nam Đế
l-nam.summary: Founding emperor of Vietnam's Early Lý dynasty, ruling from 544 to 548; he had earlier been a magistrate for China's Liang dynasty.

t-nh-h-i-qu-n.name: Tĩnh Hải quân
t-nh-h-i-qu-n.summary: Tang dynasty administrative division centered on northern Vietnam from 866 to 967, which evolved into a quasi-independent regime under local Vietnamese rulers before the Đinh dynasty was founded.

d-ng-nh-ngh.name: Dương Đình Nghệ
d-ng-nh-ngh.summary: Vietnamese military governor from 931 until his death in 937 who defeated the occupying Southern Han garrison at Đại La, restoring Vietnamese autonomy and mentoring his protégé Ngô Quyền.

kh-c-th-a-d.name: Khúc Thừa Dụ
kh-c-th-a-d.summary: A local ruler, 830 to 907, who took power in Vietnam as the Tang dynasty collapsed, marking the start of Vietnamese independence from Chinese rule.

jiedushi.name: Jiedushi
jiedushi.summary: A regional military governor post created under China's Tang dynasty in 711 CE, giving holders control of armies, taxation, and appointments; powerful jiedushi like An Lushan eventually overrode the central court.

an-lushan-rebellion.name: An Lushan rebellion
an-lushan-rebellion.summary: A civil war in Tang dynasty China from 755 to 763 that briefly overthrew the government, causing massive depopulation and marking a major turning point in medieval Chinese history.

v-nguy-n-gi-p.name: Võ Nguyên Giáp
v-nguy-n-gi-p.summary: Vietnamese general (1911–2013) who led communist forces to victory in the Indochina wars, including the decisive 1954 Battle of Dien Bien Phu against France.

hou-jing.name: Hou Jing Rebellion
hou-jing.summary: The 548–552 upheaval in which Chinese general Hou Jing, after serving Northern Wei, Eastern Wei and Liang, seized the Liang throne before being defeated and killed by his own associates.

emperor-wu-of-chen.name: Chen Baxian
emperor-wu-of-chen.summary: Founding emperor of the Chen dynasty of China, who rose as a Liang dynasty general, seized power in a 555 coup, and forced the last Liang emperor to abdicate to him in 557. He died in 559.

ph-ng-h-ng.name: Phùng Hưng
ph-ng-h-ng.summary: A Vietnamese chief who led a rebellion against Tang Chinese rule and briefly reigned over Annam in the late 8th century, dying around 789 to 791 and succeeded by his son.

ch-h-n.name: Chữ Hán
ch-h-n.summary: The Chinese characters used to write Literary Chinese and Sino-Vietnamese vocabulary in Vietnam, officially used from the Han dynasty's rule until the early 20th century.

classical-chinese.name: Literary Chinese
classical-chinese.summary: The written literary form of Chinese used from the 5th century BCE and adopted across Vietnam, Korea, Japan and the Ryukyus as a shared language of scholarship and administration until the early 20th century.

ch-n-m.name: Chữ Nôm
ch-n-m.summary: A complex writing system adapting Chinese characters to write vernacular Vietnamese, used mainly between the 15th and 19th centuries by literati such as Nguyễn Du.

old-javanese.name: Old Javanese
old-javanese.summary: The oldest attested form of the Javanese language, an Austronesian language spoken in central and eastern Java and used as a literary language across Java, Madura, Bali and Lombok.

history-of-the-malay-language.name: Old Malay
history-of-the-malay-language.summary: An early stage of the Malay language, descended from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian, used before Indian cultural and religious influence reshaped it into Classical Malay.

kawi-script.name: Kawi script
kawi-script.summary: A historic script used across Maritime Southeast Asia from the 8th to 16th centuries, mainly to write the Old Javanese language.

n-gar-script.name: Nagari script
n-gar-script.summary: An ancestor of the Devanagari script, first used for Prakrit and Sanskrit, in regular use by the 7th century CE and descended from the ancient Brahmi script family.

l-c-b-t.name: Lục bát
l-c-b-t.summary: Traditional Vietnamese verse form alternating six- and eight-syllable lines, enjoyed by all social classes and used in most Vietnamese folk poetry.

song-th-t-l-c-b-t.name: Song thất lục bát
song-th-t-l-c-b-t.summary: A Vietnamese poetic form combining a couplet of seven-syllable lines with a six-eight syllable couplet, following complex tonal and rhyme rules.

qu-ng-ng-i-province.name: Quảng Ngãi province
qu-ng-ng-i-province.summary: A province on Vietnam's south-central coast, historically home to the H're, Cham and Kinh peoples, re-established in 1989 and merged with Kon Tum in 2025.

champa.name: Champa
champa.summary: A collection of Cham polities along the coast of central and southern Vietnam from about the 2nd century CE until 1832, shaped from the 4th century onward by Hinduism.

hormuz-island.name: Hormuz Island
hormuz-island.summary: An Iranian island in the Persian Gulf, occupied by the Portuguese from 1515 until the Safavids conquered it with English help in 1622.

seal-of-solomon.name: Seal of Solomon
seal-of-solomon.summary: A legendary signet ring attributed to King Solomon in medieval Jewish, Islamic and Western mystical traditions, said to give him power over spirits and animals; its symbol appears on the flags of Israel and Morocco.

srivijaya.name: Srivijaya
srivijaya.summary: A Buddhist thalassocratic empire based on Sumatra from the 7th to 11th century that dominated much of maritime Southeast Asia and its trade routes, especially with China.

central-java.name: Central Java
central-java.summary: A province in the middle of the island of Java, Indonesia, regarded as the heart of Javanese culture and today the third-most populous province in both Java and the country.

prambanan.name: Prambanan
prambanan.summary: A 9th-century Hindu temple compound near Yogyakarta in Java, Indonesia, dedicated to the Hindu Trimurti and the largest Hindu temple site in the country.

m-s-n.name: Mỹ Sơn
m-s-n.summary: A cluster of ruined Hindu temples in central Vietnam built by kings of Champa between the 4th and 13th centuries, largely destroyed by US bombing during the Vietnam War.

rudravarman-i.name: Rudravarman I
rudravarman-i.summary: A king of early Champa who reigned from 529 to 572 CE, son of a brahman father and a niece of King Manorathavarman, who received titles from China's Liang dynasty.

sambhuvarman.name: Sambhuvarman
sambhuvarman.summary: King of Lâm Ấp in Champa from 572 to 629 CE.

borobudur-ship.name: Borobudur ship
borobudur-ship.summary: An 8th to 9th-century wooden double outrigger sailing vessel of the Javanese people, depicted in reliefs at the Borobudur temple; similar ships remained in coastal trade until the 1940s.

east-java.name: East Java
east-java.summary: A province in the easternmost third of Java island, Indonesia, whose capital Surabaya is the country's second-largest city.

majapahit.name: Majapahit
majapahit.summary: Javanese Hindu-Buddhist empire based on Java that at its 14th-century peak held sway over much of Southeast Asia, before collapsing in 1527.

djong.name: Jong
djong.summary: A type of sailing ship originating in Java, used by Javanese sailors for trade and occasionally war, ranging from about 40 to 2,000 tons; the English word 'junk' derives from its name.

malangbang.name: Malangbang
malangbang.summary: Type of medieval Indonesian sailing ship, one of the Majapahit Empire's main naval vessel types alongside the jong and kelulus.

kelulus.name: Kelulus
kelulus.summary: A type of small rowing boat from the Nusantara archipelago, propelled by oar or paddle and sometimes fitted with sails for long voyages.

kedukan-bukit-inscription.name: Kedukan Bukit inscription
kedukan-bukit-inscription.summary: A small inscribed stone found in South Sumatra in 1920, dated to 1 May 683 CE, the oldest known example of the Malay language.

sampan.name: Sampan
sampan.summary: A flat-bottomed wooden boat used across East, Southeast and South Asia for transport, fishing, and sometimes as a floating home.

melayu-kingdom.name: Melayu Kingdom
melayu-kingdom.summary: A classical Buddhist kingdom in what is now Sumatra, Indonesia, known mainly from Chinese records and absorbed by the Srivijaya empire by 692 CE.

kedah.name: Kedah
kedah.summary: A state in northwestern Peninsular Malaysia, historically known by names such as Kadaram and Kataha, with a rice-farming mainland and the Langkawi islands.

tarumanagara.name: Tarumanagara
tarumanagara.summary: An early Indianized Sundanese kingdom in western Java whose 5th-century ruler Purnawarman produced Java's earliest known inscriptions, dated to around 358 AD.

mataram-kingdom.name: Mataram kingdom
mataram-kingdom.summary: A Javanese Hindu-Buddhist kingdom, also called Medang, that flourished from the 8th to 11th centuries and built temples including Borobudur and Prambanan.

tr-n-qu-c-pagoda.name: Trấn Quốc Pagoda
tr-n-qu-c-pagoda.summary: The oldest Buddhist temple in Hanoi, located on a small island near the southeastern shore of the city's West Lake.

nanyue.name: Nanyue
nanyue.summary: An ancient kingdom founded in 204 BC by the Chinese general Zhao Tuo, covering parts of modern southern China and northern Vietnam, conquered by the Han dynasty in 111 BC.

nakhon-si-thammarat.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat
nakhon-si-thammarat.summary: A city in southern Thailand that served as the administrative centre of the region for most of its history, originally on the coast before silting moved the shoreline.

dyah-pancapana.name: Panangkaran
dyah-pancapana.summary: Second king of Mataram from the Shailendra dynasty on Java (746–784), successor to Sri Sanjaya, who granted permission to build Buddhist shrines and monasteries honoring the goddess Tara.

samaratungga.name: Samaratungga
samaratungga.summary: A ruler of the Sailendra dynasty over the Mataram Kingdom and Srivijaya in the 8th-9th centuries, who initiated construction of the Buddhist monument Borobudur.

rudravarman.name: Rudravarman
rudravarman.summary: The last king of Funan, known by this name from both Khmer and Chinese historical records.

l-thi-n-b-o.name: Lý Thiên Bảo
l-thi-n-b-o.summary: Older brother of Lý Nam Đế who took over resistance against Liang dynasty forces after his brother fell ill, dying in 555 without an heir.

tugu-inscription.name: Tugu inscription
tugu-inscription.summary: Mid-5th-century stone inscription from the Tarumanagara kingdom, found in North Jakarta, recording a king's river-straightening and irrigation projects.

purnawarman.name: Purnawarman
purnawarman.summary: 5th-century king of Tarumanagara, a Hindu kingdom in what is now West Java, Indonesia, known for stone inscriptions describing a major irrigation project.

inh-b-l-nh.name: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh
inh-b-l-nh.summary: Founding emperor of Vietnam's Đinh dynasty, ruling 968 to 979, who unified the country by defeating rival warlords and renamed it Đại Cồ Việt.

emperor-wen-of-sui.name: Emperor Wen of Sui
emperor-wen-of-sui.summary: Founding emperor of China's Sui dynasty (541–604), a Buddhist ruler who reunified China in 589 after nearly three centuries of division and began the Grand Canal.

h-u-l-nam.name: Lý Phật Tử
h-u-l-nam.summary: Last king of Vietnam's Early Lý dynasty (c. 518–602), known by the title Hậu Lý Nam Đế, who ruled the kingdom of Vạn Xuân from 571 to 602.

sui-early-l-war.name: Liu Fang
sui-early-l-war.summary: Sui dynasty general who led the invasion force that conquered the Vietnamese Former Lý kingdom in 602, taking its ruler captive.

v-ravarman.name: Vīravarman
v-ravarman.summary: A king of Chenla, an early Southeast Asian kingdom.

harihara.name: Harihara
harihara.summary: Hindu concept and image combining the deities Vishnu and Shiva as one Ultimate Reality, appearing in Advaita Vedanta thought and in cave sculptures since the 6th century.

manusmriti.name: Manusmriti
manusmriti.summary: A major Hindu legal text dated from the 2nd century BCE to the 2nd century CE, laying out rules on caste and other duties, later influential in kingdoms in Cambodia and Indonesia.

kshatriya.name: Kshatriya
kshatriya.summary: One of the four varnas, or social orders, of Hindu society, associated with the ruling and warrior aristocracy.

history-of-hinduism.name: Hindu synthesis
history-of-hinduism.summary: The blending of diverse Indian religious cultures and traditions, with no single founder, into what became Hinduism around the beginning of the Common Era.

theravada.name: Theravada
theravada.summary: Buddhism's oldest surviving school, preserving its teachings in the Pali Canon; as of 2010 it made up 36% of Buddhists worldwide, compared to Mahayana's 53%.

mahayana.name: Mahayana
mahayana.summary: The largest branch of Buddhism, developed in India from around the 1st century BCE, distinguished by its own scriptures and its ideal of the bodhisattva who seeks buddhahood to save all beings.

brahmin.name: Brahmins
brahmin.summary: The priestly varna, the highest of Hindu society's four traditional social classes, traditionally serving as priests and spiritual teachers.

jayavarman-ii.name: Jayavarman II
jayavarman-ii.summary: A Khmer prince who founded the Khmer Empire and became its first ruler, reigning about 802 to 850 CE; he declared independence from Java and founded several capitals.

phnom-kulen.name: Phnom Kulen
phnom-kulen.summary: Mountain range in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia, also known as Kulen Mountain.

devaraja.name: devaraja
devaraja.summary: The concept of the divine "god-king" in ancient and medieval India and Southeast Asia, used to justify a monarch's rule and inspiring monuments such as Angkor Wat.

keith-taylor-historian.name: Keith W. Taylor
keith-taylor-historian.summary: American historian, born 1946, who specializes in pre-colonial Vietnamese history and teaches at Cornell University; he served as a US soldier in Vietnam.

shaivism.name: Shaivism
shaivism.summary: A branch of Hindu tradition worshipping Shiva as the supreme being, rooted in Vedic worship of Rudra, which became dominant in several Hindu kingdoms and later spread into Southeast Asia.

chalukya-dynasty.name: Chalukya dynasty
chalukya-dynasty.summary: An Indian dynasty, split into three related branches, that ruled large parts of southern and central India from the 6th to the 12th centuries and is seen as a golden age in Karnataka's history.

shiva.name: Shiva
shiva.summary: One of the principal deities of Hinduism, worshipped as the Supreme Being in Shaivism and known as 'the Destroyer' within the Hindu trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu.

angkor.name: Angkor
angkor.summary: The capital city of the Khmer Empire in present-day Cambodia, flourishing from about the 9th to the 15th centuries and home to numerous temples, including Angkor Wat.

brahma.name: Brahma
brahma.summary: A Hindu god called 'the Creator' within the Trimurti alongside Vishnu and Shiva, linked to creation, knowledge and the Vedas, though rarely worshipped today.

vishnu.name: Vishnu
vishnu.summary: One of the principal deities of Hinduism, known as the Preserver, one of the trio with Brahma the creator and Shiva the destroyer.
